name: The Duyfken to Cape York
summary: Looking for gold and trade south of New Guinea, the small Dutch ship Duyfken follows the coast into what Willem Janszoon takes for part of New Guinea. It is the west coast of Cape York: the first recorded European landfall in Australia. After clashes with the people of the Wenlock River, where a sailor is killed, he turns back at a cape he calls Keerweer, Turn Again.

stops.note: The nutmeg islands, the Company's eastern base.
Along a low, swampy coast past the Torres Strait without seeing it.
The first recorded European landing on Australia; men going ashore are attacked.
He reports the land barren and its people hostile.
